transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Kyros Head of ML), Tom Rivera (Kyros Infra), Elena Kuznetsova (Kyros Security)

Summary: quick discovery on latency/throughput needs, p95 targets, concurrency, streaming and whether Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private fits Kyros' compliance and cost constraints. Requested a 48-hour p95 token/sec bench on Dedicated and docs for SOC2/KMS.

Topics: p95 targets, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming, token/sec benchmarks, Dedicated capacity, private VPC, audit logs, model fallbacks.

Transcript:
00:00 Avery: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro - i'm avery, AE on the infra team, with ravi our se. could you do a quick run-through of your use case?
00:14 Maya: sure, yeah. thanks. so at kyros we're building a realtime fraud detection assistant that annotates transactions and writes a short rationale. 90% of inference is sub-1s per request target, but our p95 needs are around 600ms for short prompts, and maybe up to 1.2s for longer contexts.
00:33 Tom: concurrency is important - we need sustained 1k concurrent requests during peak window, roughly 250 tokens per response on average. ideally streaming so downstream user ui shows progressive updates.
00:49 Ravi: okay got it, p95 600ms for short, 1.2s for longer, 1k concurrency, ~250 tokens per response. are you currently measuring tokens/sec from your service?
01:02 Maya: we have some rough metrics. our internal bench shows around 120k tokens/sec aggregate on our current cluster (mixed A100s), but those are with batching and a custom triton setup. curious about token/sec on redwood hosted vs dedicated.
01:18 Avery: perfect. quick distinction - Hosted is easiest to get started, but Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, and Private gives you VPC/on-prem for compliance. Dedicated also lets you pick autoscale and burst configs. for p95 we usually baseline with our token/sec bench and streaming profiles.
01:34 Elena: security wise we need SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), customer-managed KMS, and audit logs retained for 1 year. also data residency - europe region for EU customers.
01:48 Avery: yea, we have SOC2 docs, SAML SSO, and KMS options. i'll send the SOC2 and private deployment checklist after this call (link: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf).
02:01 Tom: for cost, we care about per-token cost at 120k tokens/sec sustained - what's the economics on Dedicated vs Hosted? also fallback strategy if capacity taxed.
02:13 Ravi: good q. Hosted does per-token pricing, good for variable load; Dedicated is a monthly reserved pool and gives predictable unit costs - we can run a model/quantization configuration that hits your p95 with lower cost. we can also set routing policies: prefer Dedicated, fallback to Hosted if Dedicated is saturated, or route to cheaper quantized variants.
02:34 Maya: can you give an example p95 bench? like for a 13B dense model, what's p95 at 250 tokens at 1k concurrency on Dedicated?
02:46 Ravi: rough numbers, very rough: on a dedicated pool with H100-like hardware and optimized kernels, p50 might be ~50ms per request for short contexts, p95 for 250 tokens at 1k concurrency depends a lot on batching and KV-cash - i mean, KV-cache - and streaming overhead. we typically run token/sec bench with both streaming and non-streaming paths to capture overhead, and report p95 latencies.
03:12 Tom: we care about tail latency, not just avg. our SLOs are p95 under 700ms for <100 token responses, p95 under 1.2s for 250 tokens.
03:24 Ravi: understood. we can architect batching so that short requests avoid waiting behind long ones: priority queues and shard by route. we also have prefix caching to handle repeated prompts - that improves effective tokens/sec.
03:38 Maya: what about streaming - does streaming add overhead that will push p95 from 600ms to 900ms?
03:46 Ravi: there's a slight hit - the streaming path has more frequent flushes and can increase p95 by ~10-30% depending on chunk size. but you can tune chunking and early-token flush to reduce visible latency. we'll test with your real prompts.
04:02 Elena: how do you measure concurrent tokens/sec? do you have tooling or sample benchmark scripts?
04:08 Ravi: yes we have a bench harness and example configs. we'll provide a benchmark runbook and a script that replays your traffic traces. we'll also run a 48-hour p95 token/sec bench on Dedicated to show stability under real load.
04:23 Maya: ok cool. our concerns: 1) latency SLOs, 2) cost predictability, 3) compliance. if Dedicated can meet p95 at 1k concurrency sustainably and you provide fallback to hosted during incidents, that's ideal.
04:37 Avery: totally. next steps: we'll send pricing, SOC2/KMS docs, and a benchmark worksheet. can you share a sample traffic trace and prompt distributions?
04:48 Maya: yes i'll share traces. one more question - for private deployment, is on-prem realistic for our team or is VPC preferred? we have some regulated customers in EU, so VPC in eu-west-1 is fine but some legacy customers require on-prem.
05:03 Ravi: Private on-prem is possible but it's a longer sales + ops cycle. VPC/private control plane in a cloud region is faster and supports KMS/HSM integrations. on-prem needs packaging and could add weeks to months depending on network and airgap.
05:18 Tom: what about model fallbacks and quantized variants - how disruptive is switching from an fp16 variant to a quantized 4-bit at runtime?
05:26 Ravi: we've built automatic fallback policies that switch to a compatible quantized variant when capacity is low. quality delta depends on model; for many workloads 4-bit LLMQ gives near-equal output, but we recommend running evals. we surface quality/regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
05:44 Maya: security question - audit logs: do you provide token-level logs? we need to show who called what and the prompt hash, but not store raw PII.
05:56 Avery: we can provide detailed request logs with redaction options and hashed prompts, plus long-term retention add-on. i'll include the audit log doc link in follow-up.
06:06 Tom: ok let's talk numbers. what's a realistic Dedicated pool size to hit 1k concurrency at p95 700ms for 250 tokens?
06:16 Ravi: i need to run the bench with your traces, but ballpark: an H100-like pool with ~16-32 GPUs with optimized batching might be in the right order. again depends on model size and quantization; if you pick a smaller 13B quantized model, you can reduce GPUs.
06:33 Maya: examples would be great. also, we want to test streaming throughput - can the 48-hour bench include streaming mode with client-side chunk size of 256 tokens?
06:45 Ravi: yes, we'll configure streaming chunking, and measure p95 across both streaming and non-streaming endpoints, plus tokens/sec aggregate and per-route breakdown.
06:55 Elena: any compliance gotchas for EU residency and KMS?
07:01 Avery: we can provision Dedicated in eu-west-1 and plug in customer-managed KMS/HSM. Private VPC also supports customer KMS. i'll include the integration notes.
07:11 Maya: great. okay just to recap and avoid misunderstanding. can we do a quick recap?
07:16 Avery: sure. recap: 1) Kyros SLOs: p95 600ms short, 1.2s long; target concurrency 1k; avg response ~250 tokens. 2) Redwood will: send SOC2 and private deployment checklist, provide pricing and Dedicated configuration examples, run 48-hour Dedicated p95 token/sec benchmark in streaming+non-streaming modes using Kyros traces, and propose fallback/routing policies. 3) Kyros to share traffic traces and prompt distributions and confirm compliance constraints.
07:49 Maya: yes that's correct. thanks.
07:52 Avery: cool - we will follow up. thanks everyone.
